title: Product Appeal Audit Spec
description: Structured, already-scored input for scripts/appeal_audit.mjs. Every field is a number, boolean, or enum the analyst decided during the Analysis Process in SKILL.md; the auditor never inspects free text, images, or URLs itself. The technicalDocument and surfer blocks are optional and absent for an ordinary landing page.

personas.description: One entry per target persona, each with the Desirability Triangle sub-scores from the Analysis Process (Step 2).

fiveSecondTest.description: Whether each of the 5-Second Test's four questions was clear within ~5 seconds (SKILL.md 'Quick Analysis: The 5-Second Test').

category.description: Visitor could identify what this is.

forWho.description: Visitor could identify who it's for.

promise.description: Visitor could identify the core promise.

cta.description: Visitor could identify what to do next.

objectionsAddressed.description: Whether each standard objection type from the Objection Map (Step 3) is addressed on the page.

trustLadderViolation.description: True if the page asks for account creation/payment before demonstrating value (Trust Ladder Violation anti-pattern).

identityMismatch.description: True if the analyst judges the page tries to visually/verbally appeal to too many distinct identities, independent of persona count.

featureSoupHeadline.description: True if the headline lists 3+ capabilities/buzzwords instead of one outcome (Feature Soup Headline anti-pattern).

screenshotHero.description: True if the hero image is a bare product screenshot with no outcome/context (Screenshot Hero anti-pattern).

surfaceKind.description: What is being evaluated. A wireframe can FAIL appeal but cannot PASS it: language, visual identity, tone, and real social proof are not present to be scored. See references/surface-appeal-adapters.md.

technicalDocument.description: Appeal fields specific to papers, monographs, textbooks, and technical whitepapers. See references/technical-document-appeal.md.

shelfTest.description: The 30-Second Shelf Test: the technical analogue of the 5-Second Test. Five questions, because a technical reader has a real alternative and a real cost.

subject.description: Reader could say what this is about.

audience.description: Reader could say who it is for, and whether that is them.

promise.description: Reader could say what they will be able to do after.

cost.description: Reader could say what it costs: length, difficulty, assumed background.

differentiation.description: Reader could say why this rather than the standard reference.

returnOnEffort.description: The fourth vertex the Desirability Triangle grows when the price is forty hours instead of thirty seconds.

timeToFirstInsightSeconds.description: Seconds of reading before the first payoff, for the readers who reach it. ux-friction-analyzer's scripts/surfer_model.mjs computes this exactly as payoffReach[].expectedSecondsToReach.

patienceBudgetSeconds.description: How long this reader gives the document before the decision to continue is re-made. Say in the report where the number came from.

costTransparency.description: Does it state what it will cost — length, difficulty, required background? 0-10.

payoffVisibility.description: Can the reader see the destination from where they are standing? 0-10.

audienceDeclared.description: False if the document never states who it is for. 'For researchers and practitioners alike' counts as false.

prerequisitesDeclared.description: False if required background is never stated.

prerequisitesHonest.description: False if the stated prerequisites understate what the hardest load-bearing section actually assumes.

resultStatedInAbstract.description: False for a structural abstract that describes organisation ('In Section 2 we...') instead of the finding.

contributionLocatable.description: False if a reader cannot tell what is new here versus what is standard.

figuresSelfContained.description: False if figures need the surrounding prose to be understood — the technical form of the Screenshot Hero anti-pattern.

limitationsStated.description: False if there is no limitations section, or one that names no real weakness (only future work).

reproducibilityArtifacts.description: Strongest reproducibility evidence offered. A repository with a README and no runnable code is 'none', not 'code-only'.

typographicCraft.description: Consistency of notation, quality of mathematical setting, figure production. On technical material this is the trust triangle's 'professional execution' row doing more work than anywhere else.

readerMap.description: The routes the document prints for named kinds of reader - a "Reader's Map", a "How to read this book", role tracks on a docs site. Friction asks whether each route works (ux-friction-analyzer's readerPaths); this asks whether it was worth walking, and whether the persona it names is one being scored.

declared.description: False if the document never tells readers how to read it.

discoverable.description: False if the map exists but sits where only a linear reader will find it - which is the readers who did not need it.

paths.description: One entry per printed route. Numeric fields are read straight from ux-friction-analyzer's per-route readout (readout.readerPaths[]).

id.description: Route identifier, matching the readerPaths entry in the surface graph.

persona.description: The persona this route addresses. Joined to personas[].name as a key - it must correspond exactly, up to case and surrounding whitespace. A route naming a persona that is not scored, or a scored persona with no route, is a finding.

payoffReachProbability.description: Fraction of the readers who take this route that reach its payoff.

completion.description: Fraction that reach the end of the route. Never read this alone: a shorter route completes more and teaches less.

timeToFirstInsightSeconds.description: Seconds of reading along this route before its payoff.

patienceBudgetSeconds.description: THIS reader's budget, which is usually not the book's.

brokenPrerequisiteCount.description: Concepts the route needs that it routes past - readout.readerPaths[].brokenByMap.length from the friction skill.

payoffMatchesPersona.description: False if what the route delivers is not what the persona it names came for.

surfer.description: Readout handed over from ux-friction-analyzer's scripts/surfer_model.mjs, run on the same surface. Appeal and friction are two readouts of one chain.

readerMode.description: Which surfer produced these numbers. Report skim for a document: nobody starts in study mode.

payoffReachProbability.description: Fraction of arrivals that ever reach a payoff node.

completion.description: Fraction of arrivals that reach the end.
